draft.title: Keeping connection in view, then stepping back

sections.heading: Trying to influence what happens next
sections.text: When a disagreement makes the next step feel uncertain, the Explaining response keeps your point in view. It is trying to shape what happens next; underneath is a concern about losing contact or not knowing where you stand. Its work is preventive: keep the connection in view while the outcome is still unsettled.

sections.heading: When explaining stops helping
sections.text: When explaining is no longer helping, you shift to leaving or ending the exchange. At that point the aim changes: you want the feeling to ease, and afterward it becomes easier to bear. The Step-back response changes the job from trying to influence what happens next to getting some room from the immediate feeling. The shift is clear in this disagreement; whether it reflects one response changing course or two separate inner parts remains open.

claims.text: In the recalled disagreement, you kept explaining your point when it became tense.

scope.description: One actual-recalled disagreement; no fixed lookback window is defined.

claims.rationale: Current D61.explain observation: the selected option says the respondent kept explaining their point as the disagreement became tense.
remaining_uncertainty: This single recalled occurrence does not establish frequency or a stable trait.

claims.text: While explaining, you were trying to influence what happened next and were concerned about losing contact or not knowing where you stood.

scope.description: One actual-recalled disagreement; D02 is bound to the D61 response in this occurrence.

claims.rationale: D02.prevent states an aim to change what might happen next; D03.connection names losing contact or not knowing where things stood as the most concerning outcome.
remaining_uncertainty: The packet does not establish the other person's actual intentions or the eventual relational outcome.

claims.text: After the explanation was not helping, you left or ended the exchange.

scope.description: One actual-recalled disagreement; a respondent-reported before relation connects the first and next steps.

claims.rationale: D07.leave records the next action. D08.after_failed supplies the only reported order edge: the second response began after the first was not helping; the edge is temporal and does not establish causality.
remaining_uncertainty: The packet does not establish that leaving was caused by the first move or that this order recurs.

claims.text: At the next point, you wanted the feeling to ease right then; immediately after the next response it became easier to bear.

scope.description: The next step of the same actual-recalled disagreement.

claims.rationale: D09.relief states the desired immediate easing, and D10.relief reports that the feeling became easier to bear immediately after the next response.
remaining_uncertainty: The response and relief are temporally linked in the report; the packet does not prove that leaving caused the change.

claims.text: In this disagreement, explaining functioned as a preventive attempt to influence the next relational outcome and reduce the risk of losing contact or remaining unsure where things stood.

scope.description: A bounded interpretation of the first response in one actual-recalled disagreement.

claims.rationale: The actual action is linked to a stated aim and a named feared relational outcome. The interpretation describes the local job of the response, not a distinct enduring part or a confirmed successful outcome.
remaining_uncertainty: One occurrence cannot establish recurrence, a permanent part identity, or the other person's intentions.

claims.text: After the explaining response was not helping, stepping out was a context-bound next move oriented toward immediate emotional relief.

scope.description: A bounded interpretation of the next response in the same actual-recalled disagreement.

claims.rationale: D07 and D08 bind stepping out to the next position after the earlier explanation was not helping; D09 names immediate easing as the next aim and D10 reports easier-to-bear feeling after the next response. This supports a local function, not a causal certainty or enduring role.
remaining_uncertainty: It is not established whether the two response functions are one response changing course or two separate inner parts.
This is not evidence of a recurrent loop or a general rule that leaving is protective.
